Evidence contradicts the provisional NO as a whole-order status. I read the complete held order (89 FR 60791-60792): Sec. 1 establishes the emergency board; Sec. 2 sets the 30-day report deadline; Sec. 3 imposes a 120-day status-quo duty; Sec. 5 terminates the Board on submission of its report (EO 14128 of 2024-11-21, held, recites that it did terminate, but not when). But Sec. 4 (Records Maintenance) says the Board's records 'are records of the Office of the President and upon the Board's termination shall be maintained in the physical custody of the National Mediation Board', a standing custody direction with no stated end.

Unless that retained independent command is shown to have ended, no whole-order end exists and the NO status is not supported; if it is treated as spent, the Board's report date (not held) is still needed to date Sec. 5 and the 120-day period (ending about 2024-11-22 on the order's own count). Reported to the coordinator; the ledger status is not changed.
